source_facts.text: Maxwell separates decaying from growing disturbances, including oscillatory cases. He describes governor adjustment becoming too strong for stable motion. His continuous mechanical analysis does not establish the thresholds of the discrete example below.

The authors acknowledge a broader return-of-output usage, then restrict feedback to error-controlled negative feedback. Their overshoot account says inadequate damping can make feedback positive at particular frequencies. Preserve that qualification.
Ashby uses feedback for mutual effects, discusses a narrower return-connection usage, and warns that circuit accounts alone do not determine the behaviour of richly interconnected wholes.

Ashby specifies essential variables and acceptable states; protection may be passive or active. He distinguishes response to a threatened disturbance from error-based correction. His acceptable set is given outside the analysis; useful partial regulation can permit small errors.

proposed_profile.title: Feedback
proposed_profile.canonical_definition: A circular causal or informational relation in which an output or consequence affects later input, state or action. The sign, delay, reference condition and mechanism must be stated.
proposed_profile.summary: Feedback is not merely receiving comments. It is a circular relation in which consequences return to influence what happens next. The loop may counteract change, reinforce it, oscillate, delay response or fail because no actor can use the returned information. A correction sign, a stable response, and acceptable performance are separate questions. Historical authors also used different boundaries for the term.
proposed_profile.why_it_matters: Systems work often says feedback when it means reporting, evaluation, data or learning. Those are only feedback when they close a loop that can alter subsequent action. Sign, delay, reference condition and response capacity determine what the loop actually does.

proposed_profile.title: Regulation
proposed_profile.canonical_definition: A relation among disturbances, a reguland, a regulator and acceptable outcomes in which outcome variety is constrained relative to a stated goal or essential-variable range.
proposed_profile.summary: Regulation is the work of keeping outcomes within acceptable ranges despite disturbance. It may operate through feedback, anticipation, constraints, buffering, redundancy, local autonomy or changes to the environment. Specify the essential variables, acceptable set, and disturbance conditions. Ashby distinguishes passive protection, response to a threatened disturbance, and error-based correction; an error need not imply that useful regulation has failed.
proposed_profile.why_it_matters: Regulation is often collapsed into command and control. Ashby instead asks what variety of disturbance reaches the system, what responses are available and which outcomes count as acceptable. The regulator may be distributed rather than a boss or central unit.
proposed_profile.key_distinctions: ["regulation vs domination", "regulator vs manager", "acceptable range vs one fixed target", "distributed vs central regulation", "regulation vs optimisation", "passive protection vs disturbance-based response vs error-based correction", "given acceptable set vs agreement about what ought to count as acceptable", "exact error elimination vs useful partial regulation"]

original_model.fixed_conditions: r=0 and k fixed per run; exact immediate measurement; integrating state update; one initial displacement; no additional plant/delay dynamics, noise, saturation, or subsequent disturbance.
original_model.meaning: This is original exposition, not an equation taken from Maxwell, Rosenblueth/Wiener/Bigelow, or Ashby. Gain and step have no calibrated organisational or physical units.
original_model.analytic_result: From a nonzero initial error, error tends to zero exactly for0<k<2. k=0 preserves error; k=1 reaches exact zero in one step; k=2 has undamped alternation; k>2 grows in magnitude. Initial zero remains zero for every shown gain and does not prove stability.
original_model.performance_result: An inclusive tolerance-band test includes the initial state and only the chosen finite horizon. It is separate from analytic stability. Finite JavaScript values and rounded display are disclosed.
original_model.moving_target_limit: If r varies, e[n+1]=(1-k)e[n]+r[n+1]-r[n]; the fixed-target result alone does not establish tracking.
original_model.model_assumption_not_a_claim: No actual queue, service, organisational response, medical mechanism, or causal field result is inferred.
